Individuals and entities who paid a $30 administrative fee for a red-light camera violation in Suffolk County, New York, at any point from April 1, 2013, to the present may be eligible to submit a claim for up to $36 per violation from a class action settlement.

Class members are individuals or entities who paid a $30 administrative fee between April 1, 20213, and the present to Suffolk County or the Suffolk County Traffic and Parking Violation Agency for a red-light camera program violation.

Cash payment: Class members can submit a claim to receive a cash payment of up to $36 for each administrative fee paid for a red-light camera violation during the qualifying period. The settlement administrator will determine the final payment amount by the total number of claims filed.

To receive a settlement payment, class members can file a claim online or print and complete the PDF claim form and mail it to the settlement administrator.

Individuals or entities that do not know their class member ID can obtain one by submitting a contact us form online or contacting the settlement administrator at 833-447-6790.

To submit a claim online or by mail, class members must provide the class member ID from the settlement notice they received or obtained from the settlement administrator.

https://www.claimdepot.com/settlements/t.page_title: Twin Cities Pain Clinic Data Breach Class Action Settlement
https://www.claimdepot.com/settlements/t.summary:
Individuals whose private information unauthorized individuals accessed or acquired in the July 2025 data incident at Twin Cities Pain Clinic may be eligible to claim up to $4,500 and two years of credit monitoring from a class action settlement.

Class members are all individuals in the United States whose private information the July 2025 data incident at Twin Cities Pain Clinic may have exposed.

Eligible class members will receive the following benefits:

Extraordinary losses: Individuals who experienced actual, documented out-of-pocket losses due to the data incident can claim up to $4,500 for extraordinary losses, such as identity theft or fraud. The losses must have occurred between July 9, 2025, and Nov. 9, 2026.

Ordinary losses: Class members who did not incur extraordinary losses may claim up to $450 for ordinary losses, such as credit monitoring fees, costs to replace IDs and postage. The losses must have occurred between July 9, 2025, and Nov. 9, 2026.

Credit monitoring: All class members are eligible for two years of CyEx Financial Shield Complete credit monitoring, which includes $1 million in financial fraud insurance and monitoring for identity theft, unauthorized financial transactions and high-risk activity.

Individuals who received a notice about the TRC Staffing data breach may be eligible to submit a claim for up to $5,080 from a class action settlement.

Individuals who received a notice that their private information may have been impacted by the TRC Staffing Services data breach that occurred between March 25, 2024, and April 12, 2024, may qualify to claim up to $5,080 from a class action settlement. The cybersecurity incident involved more than 158,593 people.

Class members are United States residents who received a notice letter from TRC Staffing Services notifying them that the data breach that occurred from on or about March 25, 2024, through on or about April 12, 2024, may have compromised their data.

Class members have the following benefit options:

Documented monetary losses and/or lost time: Class members can claim up to $5,000 for documented out-of-pocket expenses related to the data breach plus up to four hours of lost time spent responding to the incident at $20 per hour ($80 maximum).

Alternative pro rata cash payment: Class members who do not submit a monetary losses and/or lost time claim can submit a claim to receive a pro rata cash payment of up to $200. The settlement administrator will determine the final payment amount by the total number of claims filed.

Drivers who purchased certain Thinkware dashcams between Jan. 25, 2019, and Aug. 31, 2024, may qualify to claim a cash payment from a class action settlement.

Individuals and entities who purchased a Thinkware X700, F200PRO, DC-M2-FG-IR, DC-M2-FG or F70PRO dashcam in the United States between Jan. 25, 2019, and Aug. 31, 2024, may be eligible to submit a claim for a cash payment from a class action settlement.

Class members must meet the following criteria:

They reside in the United States and purchased one of the qualifying Thinkware dashcam models between Jan. 25, 2019, and Aug. 31, 2024:

They purchased the camera for personal use and not for resale.

Pro rata cash payment: Class members can submit a claim to receive a pro rata cash payment from the net settlement fund. The settlement administrator will determine the final payment amount by the type and number of eligible dashcams purchased and the total number of valid claims submitted.

To receive a settlement payment, class members can file a claim online or print and complete the PDF claim form and mail it to the settlement administrator.

Class members who do not have a settlement claim ID must provide the Thinkware product purchased, quantity purchased, purchase location, approximate date of purchase and serial number associated with the dashcam.

https://www.claimdepot.com/settlements/w.summary:
Drivers insured by State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co. in Washington state who received a payment for property damage under their underinsured motorist property damage coverage between Jan. 13, 2019, and Feb. 27, 2026, may be eligible to submit a claim for a cash payment estimated at $625 from a class action settlement.

Class members must meet the following criteria:

The accident occurred between Jan. 13, 2019, and Feb. 27, 2026.

Class members who had more than one qualifying accident may submit a separate claim for each qualifying accident. The settlement administrator will provide a claim form for each eligible accident.

Cash payment: Class members can submit a claim to receive a cash payment from the net settlement fund. The settlement administrator will determine the final payment amount using the individual and total vehicle repair costs and the total number of claims filed. The average payment amount is estimated to be around $625 per claim.

Class members who previously received a diminished value payment from State Farm will receive a reduced settlement payment.

To receive a settlement payment, class members can file a claim online or complete the claim form included with their notice and mail it to the settlement administrator. They must submit a claim form for each qualifying accident.
